1 سَقَرَ الضْلَرRَّمْسُ , (S,) aor.
سَقُرَ , inf. n. سَقْرٌ, (TA,) The sun scorched, or burned, him, altering the colour of his complexion and shin, (S, * TA,) and pained him, or pained his brain by its heat: (TA:) melted and heated him, or it. (TA.) And سَقَرَتْهُ النَّارُ The fire altered the colour of his skin; or scorched his skin, and altered its colour; as also صَقَرَتْهُ. (Bd in liv. 48.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
